title: Spike: cloud workers on claude -p with the operator's Max subscription token
description: Operator, 2026-10-05: how well could cloud workers run `claude -p` on the Max subscription? The 'no claude in the cloud' rule (memory: cloud-off-claude-local-opus-fine) is economic — cloud claude billed per token; a subscription token changes that, so the rule would become 'no per-token claude in the cloud'. FIRST: the operator checks Anthropic's current consumer terms / usage policy for unattended automated use of a subscription (setup-token is designed for CI/headless use; Anthropic's weekly limits target always-on background agents) — record the answer on this tick before any build. Then: (1) token via `claude setup-token` (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), kept OUT of the container: the Worker injects it for api.anthropic.com via the Sandbox SDK 1.0 outbound per-host interception (umq) — never in the container env or disk; (2) the claude CLI in the worker image (the local claude-CLI exception from 43y also applies in the cloud); (3) one cloud final-review job (review-epic) on opus via claude -p — the use case: opus reviews without moving a cloud run local (hn6 2026-10-04); (4) measure latency from a Cloudflare container, how many concurrent claude jobs the subscription tolerates before 429s, and how a 429 behaves; (5) design: a capped 'claude-sub' rung (1–2 concurrent) for review/closeout (and maybe the top implement rung), stepping down to the Workers AI ladder on a subscription rate limit instead of stalling; the cloud routing rule changed in one place (tick nwn).
acceptance_criteria: [1] Terms answer recorded on the tick. [2] A staging cloud review job ran on opus via claude -p with the token injected by the Worker (never in the container). [3] Measured latency, concurrency ceiling and 429 behaviour recorded. [4] A decision doc with the recommended rung/cap/fallback design.
